pattern.top_pattern: CA acute hospital cost increase at OU Health looks more price-led than volume-led

providers: OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER

key_driver_codes: OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER
pattern.pattern_details: In CA, OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER shows acute hospital cost pressure that appears driven more by price per admission than by added volume. One rare vascular inpatient case also stands out, reinforcing that the change is concentrated in a small number of high-cost claims. The main business lever is claim and reimbursement review at this provider, with clinical validation for the outlier case.
pattern.why_it_matters: When spend rises despite fewer claims, payment terms, claim pricing, or unusually costly cases become the priority levers.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Audit recent CA acute hospital claims paid to OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER for rate application, claim accuracy, and the vascular inpatient case details before broader utilization action.
pattern.validation_reason: The operational increase is low-volume and concentrated, and the clinical driver is a single inpatient case.
evidence_summary: CA acute hospital spend at OU HEALTH UNIVERSITY OF OKLAHOMA MEDICAL CENTER rose about +$17K even though claims were down by 2.
Paid per admission increased by about +$16.6K, indicating unit-cost pressure.
A separate inpatient Med/Surg vascular case added about +$17K from 1 claim tied to diagnosis I70223.
